How Yamuna Expressway is accelerating urban expansion Given its significance as a vital corridor, numerous facilities and developments have emerged along Yamuna Expressway, establishing it as a prime location for both residential and commercial real estate ventures. Yamuna Expressway, Taj Expressway, Delhi, Noida, Mathura, Agra. residential real estate, commercial real estate, urban expansion, The Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority, YEIDA The Yamuna Expressway, commonly referred to as the Taj Expressway, is a six-lane, access-controlled roadway that spans 165.5 kilometers, originating in Delhi and linking Noida, Mathura, and Agra. As a result, it ranks among the most heavily-trafficked highways in the region. Given its significance as a vital corridor, numerous facilities and developments have emerged along this expressway, establishing it as a prime location for both residential and commercial real estate ventures. The Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) has chalked out plans to invest Rs 14,000 crore over the next five years for purchasing 6,065 hectares of land in the vicinity of the upcoming Noida International Airport for developing urban hubs, industrial hubs, public amenities, and a logistics hub along the expressway in order to attract further investment in the region. The Yamuna Expressway, engineered for rapid transit and operational efficiency, effectively links Pari Chowk in Noida to Kuberpur in Agra along NH-2, thereby connecting several key cities in Uttar Pradesh. By circumventing NH-8, it has significantly decreased the travel duration between Delhi and Agra to approximately two-and-a-half hours. The well-structured infrastructure of the expressway has alleviated congestion on the eastern side of the Yamuna, including the older GT Road and National Highway 2. Enhanced connectivity not only provides a smoother travel experience but also facilitates the efficient movement of goods for trade and commerce. Additionally, the expressway is connected to the 302 km Agra-Lucknow Expressway via the inner Agra Ring Road, allowing for a direct route to Lucknow. The Expressway has seen growth along its route by connecting the industrial hubs of Noida and Greater Noida with the cities of Agra and Mathura more quickly and smoothly, creating more high-end residential and commercial development options and having a share in the economic development of the region. Commenting on this, Amit Modi, Director, County Group, said, “The strategic location and improved connectivity via the Yamuna Expressway have massively spurred real estate development along the corridor. In tune with this reality, the region is transformed into a smart city - a region of integrated townships designed to offer quality life with world-class amenities and infrastructure. Hence, the synergy between rapid urbanization and strategic infrastructural projects is creating fertile ground for high-yield investments and quality urban living." The development of the Noida International Airport has led to a significant increase in land prices, driven by heightened demand. Three years prior, a hectare of land was valued at Rs 25-28 lakh. By 2024, this price escalated to Rs 1.25-1.5 crore per hectare. This rapid appreciation in land value along the expressway is poised to greatly enhance the real estate market and create numerous employment opportunities, as well as boost tourism in the region. The surge in land prices is anticipated to attract both investors and developers, facilitating infrastructure development and fostering local economic growth. Additionally, YEIDA is actively working on a recreational facility inspired by Central Park, reminiscent of New York, which underscores its commitment to promoting a healthy lifestyle for the community. Salil Kumar, Director, Marketing and Business Management, CRC Group, said, “The development along the Yamuna Expressway has never failed to present an ideal blend of opportunity and experience, as the growth here has been very dynamic. Rich cultural heritage combined well with modern development makes this area an ideal destination for homebuyers as well as investors. This, in turn, propels economic growth and improves the overall appeal of this region. As the infrastructure development is shaping up, there are quite a few luxury residential projects that have come in, making this one of the sought-after destinations in terms of both living and leisure.” Yash Miglani, Managing Director, Migsun Group, Said, “The Yamuna Expressway has given a major boost to the real estate and tourism in the region. With the iconic Taj Mahal, probably the most frequented tourist spot in India, the expressway cuts down the tourists' time and effort from the NCR and elsewhere, thus persuading more and more to visit the cultural and historical treasures of Agra and its surroundings. An increase in tourist arrivals will lead to a ripple effect in the real estate sector, resulting in the emergence of additional luxury residences. This development will generate more employment opportunities and subsequently bolster local businesses.” Ajendra Singh, Vice President Sales and Marketing, Spectrum Metro, said, “The overall development around Yamuna Expressway and Noida Expressway acts as a catalyst in fast urbanization, emerging as a nucleus in terms of growth in real estate investment opportunities and viable alternatives to investors for higher return on investment. With the increase in this development, the region rapidly gets urbanized with new commercial areas and residential complexes evolving across the transformation of the landscape of the area and offering modern living and retail spaces.” The ongoing and forthcoming developments are set to align with the Yamuna Expressway, which is slated for numerous projects. This will enhance the region's reputation as a center of innovation and stimulate economic growth through the creation of job opportunities and the establishment of new businesses, positioning it as one of India's most promising areas for real estate expansion.

India’s top housing markets see 5% drop in sales, 25% fall in new launches: Report A sharp increase in home prices—averaging a nearly 20% increase across the top eight cities—impacted affordability leading to a 5% YoY drop in overall sales. real estate, India’s top housing markets, leading eight residential markets, drop in sales, fall in new launches, July September 2024, PropTiger report India’s leading eight residential markets experienced a year-on-year decline in both housing sales and new launches during the July-September quarter of 2024, as revealed in the latest ‘Real Insight Residential Report’ by PropTiger.com. A sharp increase in home prices—averaging a nearly 20% increase across the top eight cities—impacted affordability leading to a 5% YoY drop in overall sales. New launches witnessed a more significant 25% YoY decrease compared to the same quarter in 2023. Key Findings: Sales: A total of 96,544 units were sold in Q3 2024, down from 1,01,221 units sold during the same period in 2023, reflecting a 5% annual decline New Launches: The number of new residential units launched in the top 8 markets decreased from 1,23,080 units in Q3 2023 to 91,863 units in Q3 2024, marking a significant 25% drop Commenting on the same, Vikas Wadhawan, CFO of REA India and Business Head of PropTiger.com, said, “The year-on-year decline in both sales and new launches reflects the market's response to rising prices. While the demand and supply for homes moderated during the April-June period due to the General Elections and a temporary slowdown in the approval process during July-August, consumer sentiment remains positive. This is driven by strong market fundamentals, which continue to encourage real estate as a preferred investment avenue." He further added, "We are observing a healthy moderation in market activity, which is beneficial for end-users as it brings about sustainable growth. Over the last few quarters, prices have increased by 3% to as much as 50% in some prime localities of key markets, affecting immediate buying decisions. However, we expect buyers to gradually adjust to the new price realities. With the festive season kicking off with Navratri, renewed buyer interest and a spike in sales activity are anticipated. The market frenzy has slowed, creating a more stable environment for end-users. Developers, particularly in Hyderabad and Pune, have also recalibrated their supply strategies to align with shifting demand patterns, while Delhi NCR continues to display robust momentum in both sales and launches. The festive season is expected to bring fresh energy as developers introduce attractive offers, revitalising the market despite recent challenges.” Major Drops in Mumbai, Hyderabad, and Pune: In the July-September quarter of 2024, Delhi NCR saw a significant sales surge of 29% year-on-year (YoY), with 10,098 units sold compared to 7,800 in the same period last year. Mumbai, while leading in overall volume, experienced a slight 1% dip, selling 30,010 units versus 30,299 in Q3 2023. Hyderabad faced a notable decline, with sales dropping 19% YoY to 11,564 units from 14,191 units. Bengaluru's sales decreased by 11% YoY, with 11,160 units sold, down from 12,588 units in the same period last year. Similarly, Ahmedabad recorded a 9% YoY drop, with 9,352 units sold compared to 10,305 units in the previous year. New Launches Comparison (YoY Q3 2024 vs. Q3 2023): In Q3 2024, Delhi NCR witnessed a robust 76% YoY rise in new launches, with 11,955 units introduced, compared to 6,810 in Q3 2023, indicating strong developer confidence. Conversely, Mumbai saw a 13% drop in new supply, with 31,123 units launched versus 35,923 last year. Hyderabad experienced a sharp 58% YoY decline, with new launches falling to 8,546 units from 20,481 in the previous year. Pune's new supply also contracted 36% YoY to 13,543 units from 21,287. Despite a quarterly rise, Kolkata saw a 61% YoY drop, launching just 1,516 units compared to 3,850 units in Q3 2023.
